title: Quantum-Device Simulation of Optical Decoherence of Hole-Spin Qubits in Self-Assembled Quantum Dots
authors: Jyun-Jie Jiang, Pericles Philippopoulos, Félix Beaudoin, Hong Guo
abstract: Spin-photon interfaces are essential for communications between distant spin qubits in quantum technologies, but the interband optical excitation can also damp electrically driven hole-spin Rabi oscillations in semiconductor self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs). We report a device-level modeling workflow that integrates realistic SAQD geometry and multiband electronic-structure analysis with models of electrically driven spin control, interband optical transitions, and open-system dynamics. This workflow enables device-level estimation of Rabi-oscillation damping arising from repeated interband absorption-emission cycles. As an example, for a gated GaAs SAQD subjected to a uniform magnetic field $B_0$ along the growth direction of the SAQD, we predict the Rabi frequency of the hole spin qubit and its damping under external illumination. At $B_0=2$ T, the calculations yield a hole-spin Rabi frequency of 37.3 MHz. When the electrically driven SAQD is illuminated by a broadband LED centered at a wavelength of 790 nm, increasing the optical power from 0.3 to 1.5 mW shortens the Rabi-oscillation decay time from 90.3 to 17.5 ns. Increasing the SAQD height reduces the electron-hole overlap and thus the emission rate, but the resulting redshift moves the interband transitions into stronger spectral overlap with the LED spectrum, thereby increasing the rate of repeated absorption-emission cycles and enhancing photon-induced Rabi-oscillation damping. The results show that geometry, spin-control conditions, and illumination spectrum should be co-optimized in semiconductor spin-photon devices.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive simulation framework to model how optical excitation causes decoherence in hole-spin qubits within semiconductor quantum dots. By integrating device geometry, spin control dynamics, and open-system master equations, the authors quantify the detrimental effect of illumination power on qubit coherence times. The results emphasize that optimizing solid-state quantum devices requires simultaneous consideration of material structure, electrical driving fields, and optical environment.
main_problem: The study investigates how interband optical excitation causes decoherence in hole-spin qubits implemented within semiconductor self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs). The goal is to understand the interplay between spin control, photon interaction, and material geometry.
main_result: Increasing external illumination power significantly shortens the Rabi oscillation decay time from 90.3 ns to 17.5 ns in a GaAs SAQD. Furthermore, geometric changes can inadvertently enhance decoherence by increasing spectral overlap with the excitation source.
method: The authors developed a unified quantum-device simulation workflow that integrates electronic structure calculations (FEM), coherent spin control dynamics (EDSR via von Neumann equation), and open-system evolution using the Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The physical system is a gated GaAs SAQD hosting hole-spin qubits. The model incorporates multiband Luttinger–Kohn–Foreman theory for hole states, EDSR for spin manipulation, and treats optical coupling via Fermi's golden rule within the Lindblad framework.
key_observables: Hole-spin Rabi frequency (e.g., 37.3 MHz), Rabi-oscillation decay time ($	ext{T}_2$), and photon-induced damping rate.
important_parameters: External magnetic field ($B_0=2$ T), optical power range (0.3 to 1.5 mW), and excitation wavelength (centered at 790 nm).
main_assumptions: The approach relies on the envelope-function approximation, and for optical coupling, an independent-particle approximation is used for interband transitions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the SAQD structure and Rabi oscillations on the Bloch sphere. Figure 2 details the comprehensive modeling workflow connecting spin-qubit simulation (QTCAD/EDSR) with spin-photon dynamics (Lindblad master equation).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the necessity of integrating multiple physical domains—geometry, electronic structure, spin control, and open system dynamics—into a single predictive workflow to accurately model optical decoherence in semiconductor qubits.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the critical issue of environmental coupling (optical noise) limiting coherence times in solid-state quantum memories. The systematic co-optimization requirement highlights practical engineering challenges for building functional spin-photon interfaces.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Side view of the truncated-pyramidal GaAs SAQD with top and bottom areas of 1253 nm2 and 400 nm2, respectively, following the experimental device of Ref. [10]. (b) Top view of the GaAs SAQD with six metal gates labeled G1–G6, which are used to tune the energy levels of the SAQD and drive EDSR when an oscillating voltage is applied to gate G6. (c) Rabi oscillations of the spin qubit on the Bloch sphere, where B = (0, 0, B0) is a uniform and static external magnetic field.

FIG. 2. The modeling workflow consists of a spin-qubit simu- lator and a spin–photon simulator. In the spin-qubit simula- tor, QTCAD is used to (a) define the SAQD structure and de- vice geometry, (b) solve the single-particle Schr¨odinger equa- tion using the finite-element method, and (c) simulate EDSR- driven spin dynamics. In the spin–photon simulator, (d) in- terband optical-transition rates are calculated using Fermi’s golden rule, and (e) the optically perturbed spin dynamics are determined by solving the Lindblad master equation. Out- puts from each step are shown in blue.
